content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium canned chicken soup is a ready‑to‑eat soup made from chicken meat, vegetables, and aromatic herbs. The lower salt content makes it suitable for people monitoring their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The quick heat‑treatment process preserves most of the soup’s nutrients.
Sodium reduction is achieved by replacing part of the salt with herbs and natural flavor enhancers.
The chicken broth is often prepared from bones, increasing collagen content.
The product has a long shelf life without refrigeration.
Metal cans protect the soup from light and oxygen, extending freshness.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt helps maintain normal blood pressure for those limiting sodium.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The soup contains vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: A warm broth contributes to fluid balance in the body.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Warm soup is gentle on the digestive system, making it suitable for people with reduced appetite.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to chicken protein should avoid this product.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some canned soups may contain additives such as sulfites, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Higher fat content in broth
items.content: Certain recipes include added fat, which should be considered in low‑fat diets.

items.title: Can material
items.content: Improperly coated cans could leach trace metals; reputable brands follow safety standards.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the can in a saucepan or microwave until boiling. Optionally stir in fresh vegetables, herbs, or noodles. Serve hot as a standalone meal or as a starter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days.
